iut_type: End Product (smart communication unit with embedded antenna, Bluetooth V4.2 smart module, Seiko Solutions)
customer_question: What level of completeness does the test hardware need? Does it need a production-equivalent case and labels, or can bare board-plus-antenna be used for testing/registration?
question_variants: Is an enclosure/casing required for the RF test sample, or is a bare PCB with antenna sufficient?
Can we submit a non-cased prototype for test and registration purposes?
actual_issue: Seiko Solutions asked what physical completeness level the test sample needed to reach — full production-equivalent unit (case, labels) or simply a bare board with antenna — since their hardware schedule was uncertain.
plain_english_explanation: Testing can be performed without an enclosure, as long as the Bluetooth transmit/receive function itself is equivalent to the mass-production version. Cases, labels, and other cosmetic/mechanical elements are not required for RF testing purposes.
consultant_answer: If the Bluetooth transmit/receive function is equivalent to mass production, testing can be carried out without an enclosure (no case needed).
decision_logic: RF/RF PHY test validity depends on the radio performance of the actual transmit/receive circuitry, not on cosmetic completeness. As long as the RF chain (board, antenna, module) matches what will ship, the absence of a case or label does not affect test validity.
final_recommendation: When customers worry about hardware readiness for testing, clarify that only RF-functional completeness matters, not mechanical/cosmetic completeness — this can relieve unnecessary schedule pressure.
risk_if_done_wrong: If a customer unnecessarily delays testing waiting for a fully cased production unit, they lose schedule time without functional benefit to the test result.
search_aliases: does RF test need full enclosure
bare board antenna test sufficient Bluetooth
